title: Python lists
text: Python lists are ordered, mutable collections of items. You can reverse a list in place with the reverse() method, which modifies the original list. Alternatively, slicing with [::-1] returns a new reversed copy without changing the original. The reversed() built-in returns an iterator over the list in reverse order. Lists also support append, extend, insert, and pop for modification.

title: Python dictionaries
text: Python dictionaries store data as key-value pairs and are optimized for fast lookups by key. Unlike lists, dictionaries are unordered collections indexed by unique keys rather than positions. You can add entries with dict[key] = value and remove them with del or pop. Dictionary views like keys(), values(), and items() let you iterate efficiently. For counting items, collections.Counter builds on the dictionary type.

title: Mars, the Red Planet
text: Mars is known as the Red Planet because its surface is covered in iron oxide, essentially rust, which gives it a reddish appearance. It is the fourth planet from the Sun and about half the size of Earth. Mars has the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, and a thin atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide. Robotic rovers like Perseverance search its surface for signs of ancient microbial life.

title: Mars, the confectionery company
text: Mars, Incorporated is an American multinational confectionery company famous for Mars bars, Snickers, M&M's, and Skittles. Founded in 1911, it remains privately owned by the Mars family. The company also owns pet food brands including Pedigree and Whiskas. Its global headquarters are in McLean, Virginia, and it employs over 140,000 people worldwide.

title: Ocean tides
text: Ocean tides are caused primarily by the gravitational pull of the Moon on Earth's oceans, with the Sun contributing a smaller effect. As the Moon orbits Earth, its gravity draws water toward it, creating a bulge on the near side and, due to inertia, another on the far side. Most coastlines experience two high tides and two low tides each day. Spring tides, with the largest range, occur when the Sun, Moon, and Earth align.

title: The Mona Lisa
text: The Mona Lisa was painted by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci between 1503 and 1506. It depicts Lisa del Giocondo, a Florentine merchant's wife, and is famous for her enigmatic smile. The painting uses sfumato, a technique of soft, smoky transitions between colors. It hangs in the Louvre Museum in Paris and is arguably the most famous painting in the world.

title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen. Chlorophyll, the pigment that makes plants green, captures light energy in the chloroplasts. The general equation is 6CO2 + 6H2O + light -> C6H12O6 + 6O2. This process underpins nearly all life on Earth by producing both food and atmospheric oxygen.

title: How neural networks learn
text: Neural networks learn through a training process called backpropagation. During training, the network makes predictions, compares them to correct answers using a loss function, and computes gradients that indicate how each weight contributed to the error. An optimizer like stochastic gradient descent then adjusts the weights slightly to reduce the loss. Repeating this over many examples and epochs lets the network generalize to new inputs.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises, eroding purchasing power over time. It is commonly measured with the Consumer Price Index (CPI). Central banks typically target around 2% annual inflation. Causes include demand-pull inflation, when demand outpaces supply, and cost-push inflation, when production costs increase. Deflation, the opposite, can be equally damaging to an economy.

title: Capital of Japan
text: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and one of the largest metropolitan areas in the world, home to over 37 million people. It became the capital in 1868 when the emperor moved there from Kyoto during the Meiji Restoration. Tokyo hosted the Summer Olympics in 1964 and 2021. The city blends ultramodern skyscrapers with historic temples such as Senso-ji in Asakusa.

title: How vaccines work
text: Vaccines work by training the immune system to recognize and fight specific pathogens without causing the disease itself. They expose the body to a harmless form of the germ, such as a weakened virus, an inactivated virus, or just a piece of it like a spike protein. The immune system responds by producing antibodies and memory cells. If the real pathogen later invades, these memory cells trigger a fast, strong response that prevents illness.

title: Fall of the Roman Empire
text: The Western Roman Empire fell in 476 CE when the Germanic chieftain Odoacer deposed the last emperor, Romulus Augustulus. Historians cite multiple causes: political instability with frequent changes of emperor, economic troubles including overtaxation, military overreliance on mercenaries, and pressure from migrating barbarian tribes. The Eastern Roman Empire, known as Byzantium, survived for nearly another thousand years until 1453.

title: Weather versus climate
text: Weather describes short-term atmospheric conditions in a specific place, such as today's temperature, rain, or wind. Climate is the long-term average of weather patterns in a region, typically measured over 30 years or more. A useful distinction: climate is what you expect, weather is what you get. Climate change refers to shifts in these long-term averages, such as rising global temperatures, not to any single day's weather.

title: Sourdough bread
text: Sourdough bread is made with a fermented starter of flour and water that cultivates wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria. To bake it, you feed the starter until bubbly, mix it with flour, water, and salt, then let the dough ferment for several hours with periodic folds. After shaping, the loaf proofs in a basket before baking in a hot Dutch oven. The long fermentation gives sourdough its tangy flavor and chewy crumb.

title: Quantum computing
text: Quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, which exploit superposition to represent 0 and 1 simultaneously, unlike classical bits. Entanglement links qubits so the state of one instantly relates to another. Algorithms like Shor's for factoring and Grover's for search could outperform classical computers on specific problems. Building stable qubits is extremely difficult because quantum states are fragile and easily disturbed by their environment, a problem called decoherence.

title: Romeo and Juliet
text: Romeo and Juliet was written by the English playwright William Shakespeare in the 1590s. The tragedy tells of two young lovers from feuding families, the Montagues and the Capulets, in Verona, Italy. Its famous balcony scene and themes of love, fate, and family conflict have made it one of the most performed plays ever. The play ends with the deaths of both lovers, which finally reconciles their families.

title: DNA
text: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid, the molecule that carries genetic instructions in all known living organisms. It has a double-helix structure discovered by Watson and Crick in 1953, based partly on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray crystallography. DNA is composed of four nucleotide bases: adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine. The sequence of these bases encodes the proteins a cell can build.

title: Electric vehicles and emissions
text: Electric vehicles reduce emissions because they produce zero tailpipe pollution, unlike gasoline cars that emit carbon dioxide directly. Their total climate benefit depends on how the electricity is generated: on a clean grid the lifecycle emissions are far lower, while on a coal-heavy grid the advantage shrinks but usually remains. Battery manufacturing is energy-intensive, yet studies show EVs offset this within one to two years of driving. Expanding charging infrastructure accelerates adoption.

title: The Pacific Ocean
text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth, covering about one-third of the planet's surface and larger than all landmasses combined. It stretches from Asia and Australia to the Americas, and its deepest point is the Mariana Trench at nearly 11,000 meters. The Pacific contains around 25,000 islands and drives major climate patterns like El Nino. Ferdinand Magellan named it 'peaceful' after a calm crossing in 1520.

title: Why we dream
text: Scientists believe dreaming helps the brain consolidate memories and process emotions. During REM sleep, the brain replays experiences from the day, strengthening important neural connections and pruning irrelevant ones. The activation-synthesis hypothesis suggests dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity. While no single theory is proven, research links healthy dreaming to better learning and emotional resilience.

title: Blockchain
text: A blockchain is a distributed digital ledger that records transactions across many computers so no single party controls it. Transactions are grouped into blocks, each cryptographically linked to the previous one, making the history tamper-evident. Consensus mechanisms like proof of work or proof of stake let participants agree on the ledger's state. Beyond cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, blockchains are used for supply-chain tracking and digital identity.

title: Building the Eiffel Tower
text: The Eiffel Tower was constructed in Paris for the 1889 World's Fair, designed by the engineer Gustave Eiffel. About 300 workers assembled 18,038 iron pieces using 2.5 million rivets over two years. At 330 meters, it was the tallest human-made structure in the world until 1930. Initially criticized by artists as an eyesore, it became the defining symbol of France and its most visited monument.

title: Black holes
text: Black holes are regions of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. They form when massive stars collapse at the end of their lives. The boundary beyond which escape is impossible is called the event horizon. In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope captured the first image of a black hole's shadow in the galaxy M87. Supermassive black holes sit at the centers of most galaxies.

title: Coral reefs
text: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called coral polyps that secrete calcium carbonate skeletons. They thrive through symbiosis with zooxanthellae, microscopic algae living in their tissues that perform photosynthesis and share nutrients. Reefs support a quarter of marine species despite covering less than 1% of the ocean floor. Rising ocean temperatures cause coral bleaching, when stressed corals expel their algae and turn white.

title: Python, the snake
text: Pythons are non-venomous constricting snakes found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. They kill prey by coiling around it and squeezing until it suffocates. Some species, like the reticulated python, grow over 20 feet long. Pythons are popular in the exotic pet trade despite their size and strength.

title: Mercury, the element
text: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature. Its chemical symbol Hg comes from hydrargyrum, Latin for water-silver. It was historically used in thermometers and fluorescent lamps. Mercury is highly toxic, and exposure damages the nervous system.

title: Mercury, the planet
text: Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the closest to the Sun. A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days. Despite its proximity to the Sun, water ice exists in permanently shadowed craters at its poles. It has almost no atmosphere and suffers extreme temperature swings between day and night.

title: The Great Depression
text: The Great Depression was a severe worldwide economic downturn that began with the US stock market crash of 1929. Causes included bank failures, collapsing consumer spending, and tight monetary policy. Unemployment in the United States reached 25 percent. The depression lasted through the 1930s until World War II mobilization revived industry.

title: Amazon rainforest
text: The Amazon rainforest is the largest tropical rainforest on Earth, covering 5.5 million square kilometers. It produces about 6 percent of the world's oxygen and hosts 10 percent of known species. Deforestation for cattle ranching and soy farming threatens its future. The Amazon River is the largest river in the world by discharge volume.

title: Amazon, the company
text: Amazon.com, Inc. was founded by Jeff Bezos in 1994 as an online bookstore. It grew into the world's largest e-commerce company and a dominant cloud provider through Amazon Web Services. Its headquarters are in Seattle, Washington. The company's rapid delivery network reshaped global retail.

title: Cloud computing
text: Cloud computing delivers computing services such as servers, storage, and software over the internet. The three main models are Infrastructure as a Service, Platform as a Service, and Software as a Service. Major providers include Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. It lets companies scale up without owning physical hardware.

title: Tree bark
text: Bark is the outermost layer of a tree's trunk, protecting it from pests, disease, and weather. The inner bark, called phloem, transports sugars produced by photosynthesis from the leaves down to the roots. Xylem tissue beneath it carries water upward from the roots. Some barks, like cinnamon, are harvested as spices.

title: Stock market
text: The stock market is where shares of publicly traded companies are bought and sold. Prices move with investor expectations about future profits. Major exchanges include the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. Index funds let ordinary investors own a slice of the whole market. A bull market rises over time while a bear market falls 20 percent or more.

title: Soup stock
text: Stock is a savory liquid made by simmering bones, vegetables, and aromatics in water for hours. It forms the base of soups, stews, and sauces. Veal stock is prized for its gelatin, which gives body to sauces. The difference between stock and broth is that stock is made with bones while broth is made with meat.

title: Cold War
text: The Cold War was a decades-long geopolitical rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union after World War II. Although the two superpowers never fought directly, they competed through proxy wars, espionage, and a nuclear arms race. The Cold War ended in 1991 with the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

title: Common cold
text: The common cold is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract, most often caused by rhinoviruses. Symptoms include a runny nose, sore throat, sneezing, and coughing. Antibiotics do not help because the illness is viral, not bacterial. Frequent handwashing is the best prevention.

title: Java, the island
text: Java is the world's most populous island, home to over 150 million people in Indonesia. Its largest city, Jakarta, sits on the northwest coast. The island is volcanic, with Mount Semeru as its highest peak. Javanese culture is known for gamelan music and wayang shadow puppetry.

title: Depression (mental health)
text: Depression is a mood disorder that causes persistent sadness and loss of interest in daily life. It differs from ordinary sadness in its duration and intensity, lasting weeks or longer. Common treatments include therapy, medication, and regular exercise. The condition affects more than 280 million people worldwide.
